updated_result.explanation: Each cell is enqueued at most once. The analyzer checks every nested loop in the traversal. Recognized full-grid loops cost O(R*C); a scan repeated per dequeued cell raises total work to O((R*C)^2). One scan outside the traversal adds O(R*C) to the bounded O(R*C) traversal. This bounded tokenizer match is a heuristic static estimate, not a proof for arbitrary Java code. Called helpers, library costs, and complex control flow are not analyzed; this is not a proof.

loop_costs.queue_processing: O(R*C), since each cell is enqueued and processed at most once
loop_costs.neighbor_enumeration: O(1) per dequeued cell (4 fixed directions)

evidence.aggregate_work: O(R*C) dequeued cells * O(R*C) full-grid work per cell = O((R*C)^2)
evidence.bounded_work_argument: Each cell is enqueued at most once. The analyzer checks every nested loop in the traversal. Recognized full-grid loops cost O(R*C); a scan repeated per dequeued cell raises total work to O((R*C)^2). One scan outside the traversal adds O(R*C) to the bounded O(R*C) traversal.
assumptions: The grid dimensions are R by C and the traversal is single-source.
The visited cell is marked before it is enqueued.
Queue operations and grid/visited accesses are O(1).
The direction loop executes exactly 4 times per cell.
Recognized additional scans iterate rows and columns and read a grid cell.
limitations: Only fixed-bound 4- or 8-direction loops are recognized.
Tokenizer offsets are used; this is a narrow static heuristic, not a proof.
Only explicit rows/columns full-grid scans are costed; other loop work inside or adjacent to the traversal causes the grid rule to abstain.

note: Development diagnostic only; this previously inspected case is not a fresh independent evaluation.
